intro: The honeypot caught something at 03:14. It was not an attacker. It was a message, split across every protocol the intruder could find, and by the time the red team peeled the headers off, seven fragments had surfaced, each one its own little artefact. They pinned the fragments to the corkboard above the server racks, and as the night wore on the fragments began to sort themselves into neat horizontal bands, each one settling into the only row whose width it could possibly fill. One of the interns shaded in a few squares as a joke and then went very quiet, because the marks ran down the board like a ladder and, read top to bottom, spelled something nobody had ever typed. Nobody had sent anything at all, the lead said slowly, the board sent it. The red team stared at the grid of protocols and fragments and realised the answers had been arranging the sender all along.
echo: Software with bad intentions, which is all its name means.

puzzles.title: Rainbow Table
puzzles.flavor: Three letters to a strip. The strips are in order; the sentence isn't.
hints: The sentence was cut into three-letter fragments (spaces removed) and alphabetised. Reassemble it using the word lengths; it tells you the answer.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with H.

puzzles.title: Cold Boot
puzzles.flavor: Someone wrote this out in a zigzag across four lines of the ledger, then copied each line out in turn.

blocks.text: TSSNI TOILB OHSAA HEIAN HALND TPYSA OREEG WIDNL SGLAG NSMSY CDMED PILAI AK

hints: Rail-fence transposition of a sentence with the spaces removed. Try 2 to 5 rails; the sentence tells you the answer.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with B.

puzzles.title: Man In The Middle
puzzles.flavor: Scrambled inventory. Each entry picked up one hitchhiker on the way through the machine.
hints: Each jumble is an anagram of a word from this round's theme plus one extra letter. The extra letters, in order, spell the answer.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with P.

puzzles.title: Heap Spray
puzzles.flavor: A pub quiz where every answer is a count. Keep a tally, then keep counting.

items: Continents on a standard world map
Pairs of chromosomes in a typical human cell
Years of marriage marked by a silver anniversary

hints: Each line is a number from 1 to 26. Turn each number into a letter (A = 1, B = 2, …).
To check you're on track: the answer begins with G.

puzzles.title: Rubber Ducky
puzzles.flavor: A strip of paper tape, seven holes wide, fed through the teletype in the server room.
hints: Each row of the paper tape is a 7-bit ASCII character (hole = 1, most significant bit on the left).
To check you're on track: the answer begins with W.

puzzles.title: Salted Hash
puzzles.flavor: Every flag on this line has a meaning on its own. Together, they have one more.
hints: International maritime signal flags, one letter each.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with C.

puzzles.title: Side Channel
puzzles.flavor: Paint chips left behind in the server room. The labels matter more than the colours.
hints: Each hex colour code is three ASCII bytes.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with K.

meta.title: Meta: Capture The Flag
meta.flavor: Everything in the server room has a place, and every place is exactly the right size.
hints: Each answer fits exactly one row of the grid by length; the shaded squares, top to bottom, spell the final answer.
To check you're on track: the final answer begins with M.
